what happened: Only the docker exec ... sh -c '<command>' form is allowed, so no docker cp and no stdin; file contents with single quotes (SQL literals, python) broke the outer quoting. Every file is sent as base64 and decoded on the box.
yoyo has no --version; the installed version had to be read from dpkg.
the command or file that showed it: python3 -m yoyo --version (error: unrecognized arguments) ; dpkg -l | grep yoyo

what happened: The define directory must stay flat, but the operation needs migrations/ as a subdirectory beside app.db, and cwd must exist before sideeye starts. The state went outside the define (/home/user/yoyo-state, made by hand first), the toml uses absolute paths, and setup.sh copies the flat .sql files into migrations/.
the command or file that showed it: docs/cli.md (cwd is resolved before the state directory is made); sideeye.toml

what happened: A leg-d-only control cannot exist if leg b reads all of sqlite_master: anything that stops the next apply would also be a schema change b sees. Leg b was scoped to the user tables plus notes' columns and indexes, and triggers are written down as not claimed.
A PRAGMA integrity_check leg was planned (cookbook recipe 4), but no corrupt-but-readable database that breaks only that leg could be built, so it is not a leg and is listed as not claimed.

A stronger leg d (the next apply leaves the full 0003 shape) would also go red under the leg-a control (yoyo mark -m 0003 means the next apply skips 0003, so no index is made). Leg d was kept to: exits 0 and list shows all three applied. This was found by reasoning before running, not by a run.

A killed apply leaves its yoyo_lock row; without recovery, yoyo list waits 10 s and raises LockTimeout ("run yoyo break-lock"). So recover.sh is yoyo break-lock, whose open is also SQLite's hot-journal rollback.

yoyo list always takes the lock, so the checker cannot read the record before recovery without waiting 10 s per world; the legs are judged only after recovery, and before recovery only the file list is printed.
dash has no time keyword, so timing the checker failed with exit 127.
The first run-controls.sh piped check.sh into sed, which lost check.sh's exit status; it was rewritten to save the output to a file and report the real exit before the first run.

preflight --twice refused: app.db differs between two clean runs at byte offset 16148 (yoyo writes times, uuid1 ids and the host name). app.db and app.db-journal were declared scratch; after that only migrations/ is judged by bytes, and the checker carries the whole claim.

The FAIL report names the crash point (after unlink(app.db-journal), before open(app.db-journal)) but says "(named by the checker, not by path)"; which legs were red had to be read from the world lines in the output.
